[[sn:Western Dvina]][[sn:Western Dvina]]Lado, the Guardian of the Western Dvina

The Western Dvina, also known as the Daugava River, flows through Latvia, Belarus, and Russia, serving as a lifeline for the communities along its banks. According to local mythology, the Western Dvina is guarded by Lado, the revered deity known as the Guardian of the River.

Lado is often depicted as a powerful and benevolent deity, with a regal presence and a deep connection to the Western Dvina. He is believed to be the protector of the river and its surrounding lands, ensuring its fertility and abundance. Lado is also considered the embodiment of the river's spirit, its vitality and life-giving force.

As the Guardian of the Western Dvina, Lado is revered as a deity who blesses the river and its communities with abundance, fertility, and prosperity. He is believed to oversee the river's natural cycles, from its source in the highlands to its meandering journey through the plains, and to ensure its health and vitality. Lado is also considered a patron of fishermen, sailors, and all those who rely on the Western Dvina for their livelihoods.

Lado is celebrated through rituals, ceremonies, and offerings that express reverence for his role as the Guardian of the Western Dvina. He is honored as a benevolent deity who protects and nurtures the river and its surrounding lands, ensuring its continued vitality and abundance for generations to come. His presence is believed to bring blessings of fertility, prosperity, and protection to those who revere him as the Guardian of the Western Dvina.[[Category:Oldest pages before the refresh]]
